[4:56PM] #Ajegunle #Apapa #TrafficUpdate 

Traffic is flowing smoothly from Ojo Road and Otto Wharf through to Boundary.
However, vehicular movement around Boundary Roundabout is slow due to closing-hour congestion and commercial activities, though traffic is still moving.
Mobil Road, both inbound and outbound, is experiencing free-flowing traffic.

Traffic movement out of Apapa, from Point Road to Iganmu via Marine Bridge, is also smooth.
Conversely, the movement of flatbed trucks from High Bridge to the port is slow and uncoordinated. As a result, flatbeds unable to access port facilities are being restricted to a single lane to ensure free movement for other vehicles on the second lane.

#FollowLASTMA

data.text:
📌 Governance Systems in "ASEAN" Know Your Region 🌏
From full democracies to one-party states and military regimes, ASEAN is a region of political extremes.

🔍 Which of these systems will shape Southeast Asia’s future the most?

#ASEAN #Governance #SoutheastAsia #PoliticalSystems #KnowYourRegion

🧵 Full breakdown below 👇

🇹🇭 Thailand
System: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy
Note: Strong military influence; history of coups and political intervention

🇻🇳 Vietnam
System: One-party communist state
Note: Ruled by the Communist Party of Vietnam with no opposition allowed

🇱🇦 Laos
System: One-party communist state
Note: Similar to Vietnam, governed by the Lao People’s Revolutionary Party

🇲🇲 Myanmar (Burma)
System: Military junta
Note: Formerly transitioning to democracy, now under full military dictatorship after the 2021 coup

🇰🇭 Cambodia
System: Authoritarian regime under a constitutional monarchy
Note: Effectively, a one-party state ruled by a single political family for decades

🇲🇾 Malaysia
System: Parliamentary democracy with constitutional monarchy
Note: A multi-party system, though politics can be unstable

🇸🇬 Singapore
System: Parliamentary democracy
Note: Dominated by one party (PAP) since independence; political freedoms are limited

🇮🇩 Indonesia
System: Presidential democracy
Note: One of the largest democracies in the world, with regular elections and multiple parties

🇵🇭 Philippines
System: Presidential democracy
Note: Plagued by political dynasties and corruption, but has electoral competition

🇧🇳 Brunei
System: Absolute monarchy
Note: Ruled by a Sultan with full executive power; no elections

(📸 Ref image and info by @ChatGPTapp)
